Discover New York City

Seven iconic places, with facts checked against official and reference sources.

See the places

Seven places to discover

Each card links to the source of its facts.

Statue of Liberty

A gift from the people of France, dedicated on October 28, 1886. Sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi designed it and Gustave Eiffel engineered its iron framework. From the ground to the tip of the torch, it measures 93 m (305 ft).

Source: National Park Service

Ellis Island

Opened on January 1, 1892 as the federal immigration station. Until it closed in 1954, it processed more than 12 million immigrants. The main building reopened as a museum in 1990.

Source: National Park Service

Empire State Building

Completed in April 1931, this Art Deco skyscraper has 102 floors. It is 443.2 m (1,454 ft) tall including its antenna.

Source: Wikipedia

Times Square

The area, formerly called Longacre Square, was renamed Times Square in 1904 when The New York Times moved its headquarters there.

Source: CBS New York

Grand Central Terminal

Opened on February 2, 1913. With 44 platforms, it has more platforms than any other railroad station in the world.

Source: Wikipedia

Chinatown

Chinese immigrants began settling around Mott Street in the 1870s, and by the 1890s Mott and Pell streets were lined with restaurants.

Source: National Park Service

JFK Airport

Dedicated in 1948 as New York International Airport, it was renamed John F. Kennedy International Airport on December 24, 1963.

Source: Port Authority of NY & NJ
